guardare.def: To look at; to turn your eyes towards something on purpose.

mettere.def: To put; to place a thing where you want it to stay.

spiegare.def: To explain; to make somebody understand how or why something works.

sentire.def: To feel, to hear or to smell; the one Italian word covers all three.

domani.def: Tomorrow; the day that comes right after this one.

sotto.def: Under or below; in the space lower than something else.

prendere.def: To take; to pick something up or to catch a train.

restare.def: To stay or to be left; not to move and not to go away.

arrivare.def: To arrive; to reach the place you were going to.

pagare.def: To pay; to hand over money for something you take.

passare.def: To pass; to go by a place, or to hand a thing over.

fermare.def: To stop; to make something halt, or to halt yourself.

tornare.def: To come back; to go again to the place you were before.

aprire.def: To open; to make a door, a box or a shop ready to use.

male.def: Badly, and in fare male also to hurt or to be sore.

scendere.def: To go down; to get out of a car or walk down a hill.

fuori.def: Outside; not inside the house, the car or the room.

rispondere.def: To answer; to say something back, or to pick up the phone.

chiedere.def: To ask; to put a question or to ask for something.

scrivere.def: To write; to put words on paper or into a phone.

piano.def: Slowly or softly; without hurry and without making noise.

tenere.def: To hold or to keep; to have a thing in your hands.

lavorare.def: To work; to do the job that gives you your money.

cercare.def: To look for; to try to find a thing you cannot see.

contare.def: To count; to say the numbers to know how many there are.

uscire.def: To go out; to leave a house, a room or a road.

oggi.def: Today; the day you are living through right now.

sedersi.def: To sit down; to put your body on a chair or a wall.

mangiare.def: To eat; to put food in your mouth and swallow it.

tirare.def: To pull; to move a thing towards you with your hand.

volere.def: To want; to wish for something enough to go and get it.

chiudere.def: To close; to shut a door, a shop or a bag.

proporre.def: To suggest; to put an idea in front of somebody else.

intorno.def: Around; on every side of the thing you are looking at.

vicino.def: Near; only a short way from where you are now.

portare.def: To carry or to bring; to move a thing with you.

chiamare.def: To call; to phone somebody or to say their name aloud.

salire.def: To go up; to climb stairs or to get into a car.

ridere.def: To laugh; to make the sound you make when something is funny.

coprire.def: To cover; to put something over a thing so it is hidden.

dormire.def: To sleep; to rest at night with your eyes closed.

provare.def: To try; to do something once to see how it goes.

girare.def: To turn; to change direction, or to go round something.

aspettare.def: To wait; to stay where you are until something happens.

perdere.def: To lose; to stop having a thing, or to miss a train.

lasciare.def: To leave; to put a thing down and walk away from it.

trovare.def: To find; to see the thing you were looking for.

pensare.def: To think; to turn something over in your head.

raccontare.def: To tell; to say a story to somebody from start to end.

suonare.def: To play music, and also to ring a bell at a door.

camminare.def: To walk; to go on foot, one step after the other.

freddo.def: Cold; with a low temperature that makes you want a coat.

caldo.def: Hot or warm; with a high temperature you can feel on the skin.

grande.def: Big; larger than the other things around it.

lungo.def: Long; going far from one end to the other.

bianco.def: White; the colour of milk, snow or a clean sheet.

stasera.def: This evening; the hours of today after the light goes.

insieme.def: Together; with each other and not one at a time.

invece.def: Instead; in the place of the other thing you expected.

servire.def: To be needed, and also to serve food to a table.

vedere.def: To see; to notice something with your own eyes.

bastare.def: To be enough; to be as much as somebody needs.

stesso.def: Same; not a different one but exactly this one.

basso.def: Low or short; not far up from the ground.

vecchio.def: Old; made or born many years ago, not new.

pieno.def: Full; with no room left inside for anything more.

vuoto.def: Empty; with nobody and nothing inside at all.

destro.def: Right; the side opposite the left one.

aperto.def: Open; not shut, so people or air can get through.

ultimo.def: Last; the one that comes after all the others.

primo.def: First; the one that comes before all the others.

giusto.def: Right or correct; the one that fits what you need.

pronto.def: Ready; with everything done and nothing left to prepare.

quanto.def: How much or how many; the word you ask amounts with.

dove.def: Where; the word you use to ask about a place.

verso.def: Towards, and also around a time of day.

fondo.def: Bottom or far end; in fondo means at the very end.

davvero.def: Really; used when you mean a thing is true.

finire.def: To finish; to come to the end of something.

capire.def: To understand; to see what a thing really means.

ricordare.def: To remember; to keep something in your head from before.

parlare.def: To speak; to say words to another person.

sapere.def: To know; to have a fact already in your head.

offrire.def: To offer; to hold something out for somebody to take.

indicare.def: To point at; to show where a thing is with a finger.

toccare.def: To touch; to put your hand on something.

togliere.def: To take off or take away; to remove a thing.

comprare.def: To buy; to give money and take the thing home.
